response: ["When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis. (eado:pmid:39709737 recommendation 1)","Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia. (eado:pmid:39709737)","The consensus rate for this recommendation is 100% (21 out of 21 experts). (eado:pmid:39709737)","Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first-line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness and for melanoma in situ. (aad:pmid:30392755 table X)","Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness. (aad:pmid:30392755)","The 4-point score criteria include blue-whitish veil (present, 2 points), dots and globules (irregular, 1 point), and regression structures (combinations, 1 point). (aad:pmid:30392755)","Blue-whitish veil, dots and globules, and regression structures are minor or major features that contribute to melanoma suspicion. (aad:pmid:30392755)","A blue-whitish veil is defined as confluent blue pigment with an overlying white haze. (definition)","Irregular dots and globules are defined as varied size and uneven distribution. (definition)","Regression structures are defined as white scar-like areas, blue peppering, or both. (definition)","The presence of these features, especially the blue-whitish veil, is highly suggestive of melanoma. (clinical implication)","The presence of these features may contradict a classifier's benign call. (clinical implication)"]
